title: Hypokalemia: ECG Clues and Magnesium Connection
subject: Electrolytes
preview: Hypokalemia may cause weakness, cramps, arrhythmia and characteristic ECG changes such as flattened T waves or U waves.
quickRevision: Hypokalemia may cause weakness, cramps, arrhythmia and characteristic ECG changes such as flattened T waves or U waves.
Assess vomiting, diarrhea, diuretics, renal losses and acid–base status.
Replacement route and monitoring depend on severity, symptoms, ECG findings and renal function.

sections.title: Interpret the result in context
points: Hypokalemia may cause weakness, cramps, arrhythmia and characteristic ECG changes such as flattened T waves or U waves.
Magnesium depletion can maintain potassium loss and make replacement more difficult.

sections.title: Clinical interpretation & next steps
points: Assess vomiting, diarrhea, diuretics, renal losses and acid–base status.
Replacement route and monitoring depend on severity, symptoms, ECG findings and renal function.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A normal ECG does not guarantee that clinically important hypokalemia is absent.

quiz.question: Which electrolyte deficiency can make hypokalemia refractory?
quiz.explanation: Magnesium deficiency. Magnesium depletion can maintain potassium loss and make replacement more difficult.
